scene.title: The iPhone 18: A Gift on Credit
scene.description: For Sarah's birthday, Mark offers her the new iPhone 18 at a café. He bought it on a 24-month instalment plan from their joint account. Sarah's sister Julie is with them.
scene.action: Mark offers Sarah a new iPhone 18 for her birthday.
scene.time: Saturday, 4:00 p.m. (a scenario label, not a calendar date)
context: Mark bought an iPhone 18 on a 24-month instalment plan (€65 a month) from the joint account.
Last month Sarah and Mark agreed to save money this year.
Sarah's current phone is an old iPhone 12 with a cracked screen.
scene.status: Gift in Sarah's hands; the payment plan is questioned, not refused

actors.name: Mark
goals: Make Sarah happy on her birthday
preferences: Thinks her old phone is falling apart
knows: He bought the phone on a 24-month plan from the joint account
They agreed to save this year
unknown: Whether he expected Sarah to object

inferences.text: May feel proud, then defensive when money comes up.

actors.name: Sarah
preferences: Agreed last month to cut spending
knows: They agreed to save this year
unknown: How she weighs the gift against the debt

inferences.text: “It's lovely, but we said we'd save.”
May feel touched and worried at the same time.
May keep the phone and set a budget, or ask to return it.
May stay out of it, or side with Sarah about the money.

events.description: Mark, Sarah and Julie sit at a table in the café, a gift box in front of Mark.
Mark slides the gift box across the table to Sarah.

events.dialogue: Happy birthday. It's the new iPhone 18 — your old one is falling apart.

events.description: Sarah opens the box and takes the phone out.
Sarah asks how they paid for it.
events.dialogue: It's beautiful… but how did we pay for this? We said we'd save this year.
Don't worry, it's spread over 24 months on the joint account.

events.description: Julie raises her eyebrows and looks at Sarah.

unknowns: Whether Sarah will keep the phone.
Whether the instalments fit the household budget.
What happens to the old phone.
caveats: The dialogue is illustrative demo content, not a recording or a model prediction.
Prices and plan terms are scenario facts, not market data.

conflicts.description: Mark's goal (make Sarah happy with the phone) clashes with the goal they share of saving money this year.

consequences.description: His gift is received with a question about money, not only joy.
consequences.goal: Make Sarah happy on her birthday

consequences.description: Sarah has a new phone, and a 24-month debt she did not agree to.
The household pays €65 a month for 24 months from the joint account.
The new phone passes from Mark's hands to Sarah's; the cracked phone is still in her bag.
Julie sees the gift and hears how it was paid for.
Money decisions made alone may become a recurring disagreement.
Setting up the phone moves Sarah's accounts and data to it; the old phone should be wiped.
The purchase counts toward phone sales and consumer credit; one sale has no measurable national effect.
No specific societal impact is established.
If the old phone is thrown away rather than recycled, its metals and battery become e-waste.
assumptions: The old phone is not recycled.

branches.title: Keep it, set a budget
assumptions: Sarah wants to keep the phone.
branches.summary: Sarah keeps the phone; they agree that purchases over €200 are decided together.

events.dialogue: I love it. But from now on, anything over €200 we decide together.
Deal. I should have asked you first.

goal_changes.change: His gift is accepted, with a rule attached.
Keeps the phone and gets a say in future spending.

sarah.text: Might feel relieved and happy with the gift.

consequences.description: A shared spending rule may prevent the next disagreement.

branches.plausibility: Sarah held the phone and asked about money rather than refusing; a budget rule answers her concern.

layers.name: Action or event
layers.examines: Who acts, why, their goal and desired outcome, and what happens
layers.osi_role: A networking application creates or receives information
layers.engine: The scene script (acm.scene): actors, goals, ordered events and their state changes; single sentences are parsed by MLM's phrase model

layers.name: Physical world
layers.examines: Objects, materials, movement, forces, location and energy
layers.osi_role: Transmits raw bits as signals over a physical medium
layers.engine: Scene state tracks positions, holders and owners (2D player). Forces and materials: a 2D matter.js stand-in in the Image/Video chat; a 3D physics engine (Unreal Engine 5, Chaos) is planned

layers.name: Perception and observation
layers.examines: Images, video, audio, speech, sensors and observations
layers.osi_role: Transfers frames across a local network link
layers.engine: Scene observations and who can see or hear each event. Image/video recognition in the Image/Video chat uses replayed detections; a vision-language model and detector are planned

layers.name: Consequence routing
layers.examines: Determines which world models, actors and systems should examine an event
layers.osi_role: Addresses and routes packets across networks (routing)
layers.engine: acm.scene.layers.route: explicit rules over each event's verb, type, objects and effects, plus the events each consequence cites as evidence

layers.name: Human and social
layers.examines: Goals, behaviour, dialogue, relationships and group reactions
layers.osi_role: Provides end-to-end data transport between applications
layers.engine: The script model (goals, stated positions, possible feelings, conflicts) and next scenes from the authored demo or the local next-action model

layers.name: Digital and information systems
layers.examines: Applications, records, calculations, permissions and workflows
layers.osi_role: Establishes, manages and ends communication sessions
layers.engine: Explicit state changes and calculations (rule engine: has(x, y), amounts). No external system (registry, bank) is connected

layers.name: Business and institutions
layers.examines: Organisations, operations, processes, finance and policies
layers.osi_role: Represents or transforms data, including formats and encoding
layers.engine: Obligations in the scene (debts, agreements) and the rule engine's organisation-scoped impact rules

layers.name: Society and collective systems
layers.examines: Economy, markets, society, public governance and politics
layers.osi_role: Provides network services used by applications, such as web and email
layers.engine: The rule engine's society- and country-scoped impact rules. No economic or political model yet

layers.name: Planetary and ecosystem
layers.osi_role: (no OSI layer: the outermost system every other one depends on)
layers.engine: The rule engine's earth-scoped impact rules (e.g. flying and emissions). No ecosystem model yet
